CRISPR gene editing was actually first used on humans in 2016, not 2014. The first reported clinical trial using CRISPR-Cas9 in humans took place at Sichuan University in Chengdu, China in 2016, where researchers sought to test the safety and feasibility of using CRISPR to edit the gene responsible for a specific form of lung cancer.
